title: Docusign Standard to self-hosted Documenso
summary: Docusign is expensive per seat and Documenso is a direct answer, but the legal-evidence story is where the real comparison lives.

you_lose: Docusign's name on the audit trail, which counts for something in a dispute
Twenty years of case law and enterprise procurement acceptance
Managed certificate handling and identity verification add-ons
you_gain: Signed documents stored on infrastructure you control
AGPL-3.0 with an open, inspectable signing implementation

caveats: Read this one carefully: e-signature validity depends on your jurisdiction and on the evidence you can produce. Documenso produces a cryptographically sound audit trail, but "sound" and "accepted by the other side's lawyers" are different questions.
You must supply your own signing certificate. Getting a trusted one is a cost this page does not include, because it varies enormously.
For high-value contracts, the cost difference here is small relative to the risk. We would stay on Docusign.
